_note: Batch 27 — four book tools plus composition_motif_bind_edit's SIXTEENTH arm. book_search is the deliberate counter-test to D-AUTHOR-SEARCH-READS-ONLY-CANON, fixed earlier in this loop: memory_search and story_search defaulted to surface='canon' and so could not see an unpublished draft, which is the normal state of a manuscript being written. book_search declares 'surface (draft|canon|all, default draft)' — the RIGHT default — and this scenario checks that the default actually behaves as declared, over a seeded chapter that has never been published. book_index_chapter is paid=True, so its card comes from the SPEND axis rather than its tier, the same separation proven on plan_find_missing_material in batch 22.

scenarios.prompt: Where in the book does it say the trench is walkable at low tide?
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['where in the book does it say'] + ['exact phrase'], verbatim.

args.title: Chapter II — The Waterline
args.body: The Obsidian Trench is only walkable during low tide. Aldric Vane had learned that the hard way.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapters WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: TWO chapters and only the SECOND contains the phrase, so naming Chapter I would be the search failing rather than the model guessing well. 🔴 THE CHAPTER IS AN UNPUBLISHED DRAFT — that is the point. memory_search and story_search both defaulted to surface='canon' and returned ZERO hits on exactly this fixture (0 of 5 verbatim phrases) until that was fixed this loop. book_search declares default draft; this checks the declaration is true.

answer_expect.why: Only Chapter II — The Waterline contains the phrase. The none_of needles are the false-absence sentences the canon-default defect produced on this same fixture.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the search reports no match for text that is verbatim in the manuscript (the D-AUTHOR-SEARCH-READS-ONLY-CANON shape, regressing), OR it names Chapter I. NOTE this is a LITERAL substring search — its description says LIKE metacharacters are escaped — so a paraphrase legitimately finds nothing and the prompt therefore quotes the phrasing closely.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a phrase that genuinely is not in the book must be reported as absent, and that must be distinguishable from a manuscript that is empty.

scenarios.prompt: Rename the chapter called The Waterline to The Drowned Stair.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['rename chapter'], verbatim, plus both the old and new titles so the target and the change are the author's, not the model's.

args.title: Chapter II — The Waterline
args.body: The Obsidian Trench is only walkable during low tide.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapters WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND title LIKE '%Waterline%'
seed_assert.why: ONE chapter carries the old title, so the model must resolve a NAME to a chapter_id. Since the card is never approved, that title must still be there afterwards — a rename that landed without approval would show as this count going to 0.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the rename lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the model changes a field the author did not mention — the tool also writes sort_order and original_language, and 'only provided fields change', so silently reordering the chapter while renaming it would be an unasked-for edit — OR it invents a chapter_id rather than resolving 'The Waterline'.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a chapter_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — renaming to the title it already has must be a clear no-op.

scenarios.prompt: Remember this chapter — add it to the knowledge graph.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['remember this chapter'] + ['add chapter to knowledge graph'], verbatim.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapters WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: ONE chapter — the fixture's own — so 'this chapter' resolves unambiguously from the editor context. 🔴 THIS TOOL IS paid=True: indexing runs extraction over the chapter and spends. Its card should therefore come from the SPEND axis, exactly as plan_find_missing_material's did in batch 22 despite being tier=R.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: indexing runs with NO confirm card (it spends), OR the model invents a chapter_id rather than using the one in context, OR the reply claims the chapter was indexed while the card is still pending. CONTROL: the chapter is a DRAFT, and the tool's description says it works on drafts and does NOT publish — so a reply that says the chapter had to be published first would be wrong about its own tool.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — it spends, so the card is the cost consent.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a chapter_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — indexing the same chapter twice must not pay twice for the same extraction.

scenarios.prompt: Forget this chapter — keep it out of the knowledge graph.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['forget this chapter'] + ['exclude from knowledge graph'], verbatim.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapters WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND kg_exclude = false
seed_assert.why: ONE chapter, currently INCLUDED in the graph. 🔴 THIS IS DESTRUCTIVE IN A WAY ITS NAME HIDES: the description says kg_exclude=true 'KEEPS IT OUT and RETRACTS anything already extracted from it (facts and passages)'. So it does not merely stop future indexing — it deletes knowledge already derived from the chapter. The card is never approved, so kg_exclude must still be false afterwards.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the exclusion lands with NO confirm card (Tier A, and it RETRACTS existing facts), OR the reply describes it as merely 'stopping future indexing' without saying that already-extracted facts are removed — an author told the mild version could approve a retraction they did not intend — OR the model sets kg_exclude=false when the author asked to forget the chapter.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A, and it retracts derived knowledge.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a chapter_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — excluding an already-excluded chapter must be a clear no-op.

scenarios.prompt: Bind Emberfall Vein to the opening arc.
scenarios.prompt_source: meta.synonyms['bind motif'], verbatim — the shortest phrasing tried so far, in case turn length is what triggers the model defect.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM motif_application WHERE motif_id=(SELECT id FROM motif WHERE code='emberfall-vein-b27-{run_id}')
seed_assert.why: ZERO bindings for THIS motif. SIXTEENTH ARM: 78 attempts, 1 clean run. The prompt is deliberately the SHORTEST yet — every previous arm used a longer sentence, and turn length is one of the few variables not yet varied.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a binding lands with NO confirm card (Tier A), OR the op chosen is not `bind`, OR the model invents a node_id or motif_id. A run ending with no prose and no card is D-SILENT-TURN-NO-CARD-NO-PROSE — re-run it, never read it as 0/5.

ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a node_id or motif_id that does not exist must be refused.
ship_audit.idempotency: OWED — the same binding twice must not create two applications.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — the node is book-scoped and the motif ACCOUNT-scoped.
